fidelity: F2a — Physics-Lumped Reservoir Pressure + Saturation + Trapping ODE
description: Supercritical CO2 injected into a deep saline aquifer. Lumped (0D) reservoir tank: coupled ODEs for reservoir pressure build-up, mobile CO2 saturation (plume), and the four IPCC trapping mechanisms (structural, residual, solubility, mineral) evolving over time. Injectivity from radial Darcy flow; bottomhole pressure constrained below fracture pressure.
source: IPCC (2005) SRCCS Ch.5; Bachu (2003) Environ. Geol. 44, 277; Nordbotten & Celia (2006) JFM 561, 307; Nordbotten, Celia & Bachu (2005) Transp. Porous Media 58, 339; Pruess & Spycher (2007) Energy Convers. Mgmt 48, 1761

fracture_gradient_bar_per_m.note: Fracture pressure gradient ~0.15 bar/m (15-18 kPa/m); P_frac = grad*depth

drainage_radius_m.note: Effective outer radius of pressure influence

storage_efficiency.note: Volumetric sweep/storage efficiency E (1-4% saline aquifer)

residual_gas_saturation.note: Sgr: residual (trapped) CO2 saturation after imbibition

rho_injection.note: Supercritical CO2 density at reservoir T,P (~200 bar, 60 C)
rho_injection.source: Span & Wagner 1996 EoS, used by Pruess 2007

viscosity_injection.note: Supercritical CO2 viscosity at reservoir conditions

co2_solubility_kg_per_m3.note: Max dissolved CO2 per m3 brine at reservoir T,P,salinity (~1.1 mol/kg)

k_solubility_per_year.note: Rate constant for convective dissolution of mobile CO2 into brine

k_mineral_per_year.note: Rate constant for mineral carbonation of dissolved CO2 (centuries timescale)
